problems.title: Add two numbers
problems.statement: Write add(a, b) that returns the sum of the two numbers.

problems.title: Area of a rectangle
problems.statement: Write rectangle_area(width, height) that returns the area (width × height).

problems.title: Fahrenheit to Celsius
problems.statement: Write to_celsius(f) that converts a Fahrenheit temperature to Celsius using (f - 32) * 5 / 9. Round the answer to 2 decimal places.

problems.title: Greet by name
problems.statement: Write greet(name) that returns the text Hello, NAME!.

problems.title: Is it even?
problems.statement: Write is_even(n) that returns True when n is an even number, otherwise False.

problems.title: Average of a list
problems.statement: Write average(nums) that returns the average (mean) of a list of numbers. Return 0 if the list is empty.

problems.title: Pass or fail
problems.statement: Write pass_or_fail(score) that returns 'Pass' when the score is 50 or more, and 'Fail' otherwise.

problems.title: Count above a threshold
problems.statement: Write count_above(nums, threshold) that returns how many numbers in the list are strictly greater than the threshold.

problems.title: Largest in a list
problems.statement: Write largest(nums) that returns the biggest number in the list. Return None for an empty list.

problems.title: Reverse the text
problems.statement: Write reverse_text(text) that returns the text backwards.

problems.title: Median of a list
problems.statement: Write median(nums) that returns the median. For an even number of values, return the average of the two middle values. Return None for an empty list.

problems.title: Mode (most frequent)
problems.statement: Write mode(values) that returns the value that appears most often. If several values tie, return the smallest of them. Return None for an empty list.

problems.title: Total of a list
problems.statement: Write list_total(nums) that returns the total of all numbers in the list.

problems.title: The second item
problems.statement: Write second_item(items) that returns the item at index 1. Return None if the list is shorter than 2 items.

problems.title: Look up a price
problems.statement: Write price_of(prices, item) that returns the price of the item from the dictionary, or 0 if the item is not in the dictionary.

problems.title: Count the words
problems.statement: Write word_counts(text) that returns a dictionary mapping each word to how many times it appears. Words are separated by spaces.

problems.title: Unique values, sorted
problems.statement: Write unique_sorted(nums) that returns a sorted list of the values, with duplicates removed.

problems.title: Merge two dictionaries
problems.statement: Write merge_totals(a, b) that returns one dictionary containing every key from both. If a key is in both, add the two values together.

problems.title: Swap two values
problems.statement: Write swap(pair) that takes a list of two items and returns a new list with them in the opposite order.

problems.title: Smallest and largest
problems.statement: Write min_max(nums) that returns a list [smallest, largest]. Return None for an empty list.

problems.title: Linear search
problems.statement: Write find_index(items, target) that returns the position of the first matching item, or -1 if it is not there.

problems.title: Sort a list yourself
problems.statement: Write sort_numbers(nums) that returns a new list sorted from smallest to largest. Try writing the algorithm by hand (bubble sort or selection sort).

problems.title: Binary search
problems.statement: Write binary_search(sorted_nums, target) that returns the index of the target in an already sorted list, or -1. Halve the search range each step.

problems.title: FizzBuzz
problems.statement: Write fizzbuzz(n) that returns a list for 1..n where multiples of 3 become 'Fizz', multiples of 5 become 'Buzz', multiples of both become 'FizzBuzz', and everything else stays a number.

problems.title: Square a number
problems.statement: Write square(x) that returns x multiplied by itself.

problems.title: A default argument
problems.statement: Write greet(name, greeting='Hello') that returns GREETING, NAME!. If the caller gives no greeting, use Hello.

problems.title: Apply a function twice
problems.statement: Write apply_twice(f, x) that calls the function f on x, then calls it again on the result.

problems.title: Describe a list
problems.statement: Write describe(nums) that returns a dictionary with the keys n, total, mean, min and max. For an empty list return {'n': 0, 'total': 0, 'mean': 0, 'min': None, 'max': None}.

problems.title: Any number of arguments
problems.statement: Write total(*nums) that adds up however many numbers it is given. total() returns 0.

problems.title: A function that builds a function
problems.statement: Write make_multiplier(k) that returns a new function. Calling that new function with x returns k * x.

problems.title: Is it divisible?
problems.statement: Write is_divisible(n, d) that returns True when n divides exactly by d. If d is 0, return False.

problems.title: Hypotenuse
problems.statement: Write hypotenuse(a, b) that returns the length of the long side of a right-angled triangle, rounded to 3 decimal places.

problems.title: Bags and leftovers
problems.statement: Write split_coins(total, per_bag) that returns [full_bags, leftover_coins] using integer division and remainder.

problems.title: Between two values
problems.statement: Write in_range(x, low, high) that returns True when x is between low and high, including the ends.

problems.title: Leap year
problems.statement: Write is_leap(year). A leap year divides by 4, except years that divide by 100, unless they also divide by 400.

problems.title: Quadratic roots
problems.statement: Write quadratic_roots(a, b, c) that returns the real roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 as a sorted list, each rounded to 4 decimals. Return an empty list when there are no real roots.

problems.title: SCIM 105 letter grade
problems.statement: Write letter_grade(score) using the course grading table: 0-49 F, 50-55 D, 56-60 D+, 61-65 C, 66-70 C+, 71-75 B, 76-80 B+, 81-100 A.

problems.title: Absolute value by hand
problems.statement: Write absolute(x) that returns the size of x ignoring its sign - without using the built-in abs().

problems.title: Sign of a number
problems.statement: Write sign(x) that returns -1 for negative numbers, 0 for zero and 1 for positive numbers.

problems.title: BMI category
problems.statement: Write bmi_category(weight_kg, height_m). BMI is weight / height². Return 'underweight' below 18.5, 'normal' below 25, 'overweight' below 30, otherwise 'obese'.

problems.title: Largest of three
problems.statement: Write largest_of_three(a, b, c) that returns the biggest of the three values using if statements (not the built-in max).

problems.title: What kind of triangle?
problems.statement: Write triangle_type(a, b, c) returning 'not a triangle', 'equilateral', 'isosceles' or 'scalene'. Three lengths only form a triangle when each pair adds to more than the third.

problems.title: Count the even numbers
problems.statement: Write count_evens(nums) that returns how many numbers in the list are even.

problems.title: Add only the positives
problems.statement: Write sum_positive(nums) that adds up only the numbers greater than 0.

problems.title: First negative number
problems.statement: Write first_negative(nums) that returns the first negative value in the list, or None if there is none. Stop as soon as you find it.

problems.title: Who passed?
problems.statement: Write passing_students(scores). scores is a dictionary of name → score. Return an alphabetically sorted list of the names that scored 50 or more.

problems.title: Tally the grades
problems.statement: Write grade_tally(scores) that returns a dictionary counting how many scores fall in each band: 'A' 80+, 'B' 70-79, 'C' 60-69, 'D' 50-59, 'F' below 50. Include only bands that occur.

problems.title: Longest streak
problems.statement: Write longest_streak(values) that returns the length of the longest run of equal values sitting next to each other. Return 0 for an empty list.

problems.title: Mean of a list
problems.statement: Write mean(nums) that returns the average, rounded to 2 decimals. Return 0 for an empty list.

problems.title: Convert a whole table
problems.statement: Write celsius_table(f_values) that converts a list of Fahrenheit values to Celsius, each rounded to 1 decimal, and returns the list.

problems.title: Initials
problems.statement: Write initials(full_name) that turns 'Kittisak Chayantrakom' into 'K.C.' - one capital letter and a dot for each word.

problems.title: How long is each word?
problems.statement: Write word_lengths(sentence) that returns a dictionary mapping each word to its number of letters.

problems.title: Running total
problems.statement: Write running_total(nums) that returns the cumulative totals. For [1, 2, 3] the answer is [1, 3, 6].

problems.title: Standard deviation
problems.statement: Write std_dev(nums) that returns the population standard deviation, rounded to 4 decimals: the square root of the average squared distance from the mean. Return 0 for an empty list.

problems.title: Countdown
problems.statement: Write countdown(n) that returns the list [n, n-1, ..., 1]. Return an empty list when n is 0 or less.

problems.title: Factorial
problems.statement: Write factorial(n) that returns n! = 1 × 2 × ... × n. factorial(0) is 1.

problems.title: Skip the multiples
problems.statement: Write skip_multiples(nums, k) that returns the list without any value that is a multiple of k. Practise using continue.

problems.title: Sum of the digits
problems.statement: Write digit_sum(n) that adds up the digits of a whole number using a while loop. Treat negative numbers as positive.

problems.title: Collatz steps
problems.statement: Write collatz_steps(n). Repeat: if n is even halve it, otherwise use 3n + 1. Return how many steps it takes to reach 1.

problems.title: Prime numbers
problems.statement: Write primes_up_to(n) that returns a list of every prime number from 2 to n.

problems.title: Times table
problems.statement: Write times_table(n) that returns an n×n multiplication table as a list of lists. Row i column j holds (i+1)×(j+1).

problems.title: Count the pairs
problems.statement: Write count_pairs(nums, target) that counts how many pairs of different positions add up to the target.

problems.title: Flatten a table
problems.statement: Write flatten(matrix) that turns a list of lists into one flat list, row by row.

problems.title: Row totals
problems.statement: Write row_sums(matrix) that returns a list holding the total of each row.

problems.title: Transpose a matrix
problems.statement: Write transpose(matrix) that swaps rows and columns.

problems.title: Matrix multiplication
problems.statement: Write matmul(a, b) that multiplies two matrices given as lists of lists. You may assume the sizes fit.

problems.title: A Student class
problems.statement: Write a class Student whose __init__ stores name and score as attributes.

problems.title: A Rectangle with area()
problems.statement: Write a class Rectangle that stores width and height, and has a method area() returning width × height.

problems.title: A Counter object
problems.statement: Write a class Counter that starts at 0. Method increment() adds 1, and value() returns the current count.

problems.title: A bank account
problems.statement: Write a class BankAccount starting from a given balance (default 0). deposit(amount) adds money, withdraw(amount) takes money out but refuses (changes nothing) if there is not enough, and balance() returns the total.

problems.title: Distance between points
problems.statement: Write a class Point storing x and y, with a method distance_to(other) returning the straight-line distance, rounded to 3 decimals.

problems.title: Build a Stack
problems.statement: Write a class Stack (last in, first out) with push(item), pop() returning and removing the top item (None if empty), peek() returning the top item without removing it, and size().

problems.title: Printing an object
problems.statement: Write a class Temperature storing celsius, whose __str__ returns text like 25.0 C (one decimal place).

problems.title: Counting the objects
problems.statement: Write a class Robot with a class attribute count that goes up by 1 every time a new Robot is created. Each robot also stores its name.

problems.title: Inheritance
problems.statement: Write a class Animal with a method speak() returning '...', and a class Dog that inherits from Animal and overrides speak() to return 'Woof'.

problems.title: Shapes that know their area
problems.statement: Write a base class Shape with area() returning 0, and two subclasses: Square(side) and Circle(radius). Each overrides area(). Round the circle's area to 4 decimals and use 3.14159 for pi.

problems.title: Comparing and adding objects
problems.statement: Write a class Money storing baht, with __eq__ so two Money objects with the same amount are equal, and __add__ so Money(10) + Money(5) gives Money(15).

problems.title: A GradeBook class
problems.statement: Write a class GradeBook. add(name, score) records a score, average() returns the mean of all scores rounded to 2 decimals (0 when empty), and top_student() returns the name with the highest score (None when empty).

problems.title: Count the lines in a file
problems.statement: Write count_lines(path) that opens the text file and returns how many lines it has. A file notes.txt with 3 lines is ready for you.
problems.setup_code:
with open('notes.txt', 'w') as _f:
    _f.write('data science is fun
')
    _f.write('python is a tool
')
    _f.write('practice makes progress
')
with open('numbers.txt', 'w') as _f:
    _f.write('10
20
30
40
')

problems.statement: Write sum_file_numbers(path) that reads one number per line from numbers.txt and returns their total.

problems.statement: Write most_common_word(path) that returns the word appearing most often in the file. If several tie, return the one that is first in alphabetical order.

problems.title: Append to a log
problems.statement: Write append_and_count(path, text) that adds one more line to the end of the file (mode 'a') and returns the new number of lines.
problems.setup_code:
with open('notes.txt', 'w') as _f:
    _f.write('data science is fun\n')
    _f.write('python is a tool\n')
    _f.write('practice makes progress\n')
with open('numbers.txt', 'w') as _f:
    _f.write('10\n20\n30\n40\n')
def write_lines_helper(path, lines):
    with open(path, 'w') as _f:
        for _l in lines:
            _f.write(_l + '\n')

problems.title: Read the column names
problems.statement: Write headers(path) that returns the first line of a CSV file as a list of column names. The file scores.csv is ready for you.

problems.title: How many data rows?
problems.statement: Write row_count(path) that returns how many data rows a CSV file has (do not count the header line).

problems.title: Get one column
problems.statement: Write column_values(path, column) that returns the values of that column (as text) for every data row.

problems.title: Average a column
problems.statement: Write average_column(path, column) that returns the mean of a numeric column, rounded to 2 decimals.

problems.title: Best final score
problems.statement: Write top_student(path) that returns the name from the row with the highest final score.

problems.title: Write a summary file
problems.statement: Write write_summary(in_path, out_path) that creates a new CSV with the header name,average and one row per student holding the average of their midterm and final, rounded to 1 decimal. Return the number of data rows written.
